entries.text: The slicer asked for supports; the printer applied for culinary school.
Gordon Ramsay would shut down the kitchen before asking what sauce goes with this.
The printer has successfully entered a market where nobody wanted it: shelf stable spaghetti.
Somewhere an Italian grandmother has sensed a disturbance in the pasta.
The Michelin guide has requested that you stop calling this a tasting menu.
The printer has prepared a dish best served directly to the garbage.
That is a bold interpretation of al dente for a material that never belonged in a kitchen.
The noodle factory has opened without obtaining a food service license.
Even instant ramen has better structural integrity.
The original model appears to have been replaced by a plate of angry vermicelli.
An entire spool has been sacrificed to the gods of questionable Italian cuisine.
The pasta has achieved the texture of a nightmare and the nutritional value of a receipt.
The printer mistook additive manufacturing for the Food Network.
The marinara is missing, but the regret has been served generously.
A tangled mess that makes your headphone cables look professionally organized.

A spaghetti dinner whose main ingredient is the money you used to have.
